The '''2010–11 Eredivisie''' is the 55th season of [[Eredivisie]] since its establishment in 1955. It began on 6 August 2010 with the first matches of the season and ended on 29 May 2011 with the last matches of the European competition and relegation playoffs. [[FC Twente]] were the reigning champions, having won their first Dutch championship the [[2009–10 Eredivisie|previous season]]. A total of 18 teams took part in the league.
Ajax won their 30th title after beating FC Twente 3–1 on 15 May 2011.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/13405939.stm|title=Ajax snatch title from champions Twente in decider|date=14 May 2011|work=BBC Sport|access-date=16 May 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/920045/eredivisie:-ajax-end-seven-year-wait-for-title?cc=5739|title=Ajax end seven-year wait for Dutch title|date=15 May 2011|work=ESPN Soccernet|access-date=16 May 2011|archive-date=25 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121025094807/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/920045/eredivisie:-ajax-end-seven-year-wait-for-title?cc=5739|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Teams==
[[RKC Waalwijk]] were directly relegated to the [[2010–11 Eerste Divisie]] at the end of [[2009–10 Eredivisie|last season]] after finishing the season at the bottom of the table, ending one season at the highest division of Dutch football. They were replaced by [[2009–10 Eerste Divisie]] champions [[De Graafschap]], who return to the Eredivisie after one season.

[[Sparta Rotterdam]] were also relegated at the end of the promotion/relegation playoff tournament, as they lost their two-legged play-off against city rivals [[SBV Excelsior|Excelsior]] on away goals. Sparta hence completed a 5-year stint in the league, while Excelsior played for the first time at the top level in 2 years. In contrast, [[Willem II Tilburg|Willem II]] retained their Eredivisie spot after beating [[Go Ahead Eagles]] after extra time of the return leg.

==Play-offs==

===European competition===
The teams placed fifth through eighth compete in a play-off tournament for one spot in the [[2011–12 UEFA Europa League#Second qualifying round|second qualifying round]] of the [[2011–12 UEFA Europa League]].

====Semi-finals====
{{TwoLeg start}}
{{TwoLegResult|[[Heracles Almelo|Heracles]]||4–4 ([[Away goals rule|a]])|'''[[FC Groningen|Groningen]]'''|| 3–2 | 1–2 }}
{{TwoLegResult|'''[[ADO Den Haag]]'''||6–3|[[Roda JC]]|| 4–2 | 2–1 }}
{{end}}

====Finals====
{{TwoLeg start}}
{{TwoLegResult|'''[[ADO Den Haag]]'''||6–6 ([[Penalty shootout (association football)|p.]] 4–3)|[[FC Groningen]]|| 5–1 | 1–5}}
{{end}}

===Relegation===
[[SBV Excelsior|Excelsior]] and [[VVV-Venlo]] joined the Eerste Divisie-teams for the playoffs, after finishing 16th and 17th in the Eredivisie.

====Round 1====
{{TwoLeg start}}
{{TwoLegResult|'''[[FC Volendam|Volendam]]'''|| 5–2 |[[MVV Maastricht|MVV]]|| 3–2 | 2–0 }}
{{TwoLegResult|[[Go Ahead Eagles]]|| 1–3 |'''[[FC Den Bosch|Den Bosch]]'''|| 0–1 | 1–2 }}
{{end}}

====Round 2====
{{TwoLeg start}}
{{TwoLegResult|[[FC Volendam|Volendam]]|| 1−4 |'''[[VVV-Venlo]]'''|| 1−2| 0−2 }}
{{TwoLegResult|[[SC Cambuur|Cambuur]]|| 3−3 ([[Penalty shootout (association football)|p.]] 6–7) |'''[[FC Zwolle|Zwolle]]'''|| 2−1 | 1−2 }}
{{TwoLegResult|[[BV Veendam|Veendam]]|| 3−4 |'''[[Helmond Sport]]'''|| 3−3 | 0−1 }}
{{TwoLegResult|[[FC Den Bosch|Den Bosch]]|| 4−6 |'''[[SBV Excelsior|Excelsior]]'''|| 3−3 | 1−3 }}
{{end}}

====Round 3====
{{TwoLeg start}}
{{TwoLegResult|[[FC Zwolle|Zwolle]]|| 3–4 |'''[[VVV-Venlo]]'''|| 1−2 | 2–2 }}
{{TwoLegResult|[[Helmond Sport]]|| 3−9 |'''[[SBV Excelsior|Excelsior]]'''|| 1−5 | 2−4 }}
{{end}}

[[VVV-Venlo]] and [[SBV Excelsior|Excelsior]] will play in [[2011–12 Eredivisie]].
